acquisition: Stanford Interlibrary Loan request 446721, delivered as a web scan
bibliography: Buddruss, Georg. 1979. Gṛaṅgali. Ein Nachtrag zum Atlas der Dardsprachen. Münchener Studien zur Sprachwissenschaft 38:21–39.

extraction.method: full record-by-record manual collation against 300 dpi page renders; two Tesseract passes were used only for page navigation and comparison

rights: ILL scan supplied for private study, scholarship, or research; the scan is not checked in.

scope.cdial_policy: only direct source assignments are linked; comparisons attached to secondary forms or hedged parallels remain prose
scope.excluded: three explicit Grangali non-attestations (47, 110, 166); bare lect abbreviations with no printed form; unnumbered phonological examples outside the lexical section
scope.included: all main Grangali answers to Atlas questionnaire numbers 1–167, plus every Ningalami and Shumashti form printed in the numbered lexical section, including accurately glossed commentary examples
scope.language_model: Grangali (Gng) and Ningalami (Ning) are independent Jambu languages. Both retain Glottolog's umbrella gran1245 because Glottolog does not provide separate codes; Shumashti remains Shum/shum1235.

unresolved: item 150 has a source-level semantic disagreement: Buddruss glosses the Grangali form as heel, while Grjunberg glosses the comparison as ankle; the transcription itself is resolved
item 24 is certainly called a loan by Buddruss, but his proposed Pashto source is tentative
